buttonLabel: "Discover adventures in Brazil, Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Brazil's waterfalls, the Atacama Desert, the Galápagos Islands and a day trip to Montevideo offer very different experiences. All four countries in the current selection form part of a 32-day journey across eight South American nations. Adventure activities are concentrated in only some sections; Uruguay is represented by city sightseeing.
---

## How the Brazil–Chile–Ecuador–Uruguay itinerary works

Among our adventure journeys involving Brazil, Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay, you will find a [32-day tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The main program also includes Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia. The four selected countries are part of one extensive tour, not a separate short route connecting only them.

The thematic distinctions matter too. In Brazil, travelers can add a boat ride to their visit to the waterfalls. Chile provides access to high-altitude landscapes, while Ecuador offers marine outings in the Galápagos. Uruguay, on this itinerary, is **one day of sightseeing in Montevideo**, without trekking or sporting activities. The full selection appears in the [four-country catalog](/multi-country/brazil_chile_ecuador_uruguay/), with further options under [multi-country adventures](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

## Brazil: forest, panoramas and Iguazu Falls

The opening days are spent in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). On the way to Christ the Redeemer, you travel through [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/), while the Sugarloaf Mountain excursion reveals bay and mountain panoramas from viewpoints. These are accessible city excursions and walks, not a specialist jungle hike.

At [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), a visit to the Brazilian side with a Russian-speaking guide is included. Those interested can book [Macuco Safari](/brazil/foz-do-iguacu/macuco-safari-program-forest-boat/) separately, including a boat trip toward the waterfalls, or visit the [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/). **Both activities cost extra**: appearing in the day's description does not make them part of the basic price.

This is the wettest nature section of the four selected countries. Water protection for documents and electronics is useful on the boat outing, and nonslip shoes help on the waterfall paths. The complete eight-country journey also visits the Argentine side of Iguazu, since Argentina forms part of the route.

## Uruguay: a ferry and a city tour, rather than a sporting day

Uruguay is visited after Buenos Aires. In the morning, you go to the port, board a ferry and arrive in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) for sightseeing with an English-speaking guide. Free time follows before the group returns to Argentina by ferry. Ferry tickets are included.

Scheduled stops include [Montevideo Port](/uruguay/place/montevideo-port/), [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/), the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and [Montevideo Cathedral](/uruguay/place/montevideo-cathedral/). Further details are in the [Montevideo day trip from Buenos Aires](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/).

Crossing the Río de la Plata and exploring another country in one day can be an adventure in itself, but **there is no dedicated sporting program, kayaking, diving or hiking in Uruguay**. Because the trip includes a border crossing and return to Argentina, passport and re-entry requirements must be checked for each traveler's nationality. Free time in Montevideo depends on the ferry and tour schedules.

## Chile: Atacama as the gateway to Bolivia

After the Argentine and Uruguayan sections, you fly to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), then travel via Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). An optional [evening astronomy excursion with telescopes](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-astronomy-telescope-evening/) may be available; its operating conditions must be confirmed for the travel date.

San Pedro is the preparation point for the next section: a two-day 4×4 journey through Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons toward Uyuni. The itinerary mentions elevations above 4,000 m and the risk of altitude sickness. **This 4×4 journey is geographically in Bolivia**. It would be inaccurate to describe it as a Chilean safari or guaranteed volcanic ascent.

Here, the active element is extended high-altitude driving, not intensive walking or trekking. Large changes in temperature and elevation call for warm clothing, water and a sensible pace. The next major part of the journey goes through Peru, which is not included in this selection's title.

## Ecuador: island walks and wildlife in the Galápagos

[Quito](/ecuador/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/quito-panecillo-and-equator/) includes city sightseeing and a visit to the equator line. The journey then heads to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). After arriving on Baltra, you cross to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), where a separate excursion explores the [highlands and lava tunnels](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/).

The following marine day offers two possible programs, **one of which is selected**:

- [North Seymour and Bachas Beach](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/), with birdwatching, an island walk and an opportunity to snorkel.
- [South Plaza and Cape Carrión](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/), featuring sea lions, iguanas, coastal nature and swimming.

These routes are alternatives for a single excursion day. A separate scuba-diving excursion is not specified. Conservation rules apply: stay on authorized routes, follow the guide's instructions and keep your distance from wildlife. Weather and sea conditions may affect the confirmed program.

## Assessing the demands before booking

| Section | Nature of the activity |
|---|---|
| Iguazu | Walks, waterfalls, optional boat |
| Montevideo | Ferry and city tour |
| Atacama and Bolivia | Altitude, 4×4 transfers |
| Galápagos | Boats and island walks |

This journey suits people who enjoy alternating sightseeing cities, nature days and lengthy transfers. If your priorities are exclusively sports, daily trekking or wildlife exploration without urban stops, this itinerary is not that kind of product.

Preparation should account for damp conditions at Iguazu, wind and cold at altitude, sun on the islands and border crossings. Ada Tours helps coordinate the sequence of stages, excursions and physical demands, but travel conditions must be considered in light of the calendar and entry requirements of all eight countries.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in four countries

### Is there an active adventure program in Uruguay?

Not on this tour. Uruguay is a one-day trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo, including a ferry crossing and city sightseeing.

### Is Macuco Safari at Iguazu included?

No. The regular Brazilian-side excursion is included, while Macuco Safari costs extra.

### Does the Atacama 4×4 route take place in Chile?

The opening stop in San Pedro de Atacama is in Chile. The two-day 4×4 stage through high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni takes place in Bolivia.

### Can both Galápagos island routes be visited?

The current excursion day offers one of two alternatives. Visiting both would require a separately agreed change to the itinerary.

### Do travelers have to return from Uruguay to Argentina?

Yes. The Montevideo day ends with a return ferry to Buenos Aires, so border-crossing and re-entry rules should be checked in advance.

## Why the cultural route through four cities and capitals is interesting

Brazil, Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay make an unusual collection of urban histories: Rio de Janeiro with its churches and panoramas, administrative Santiago, historic Quito and port-city Montevideo. They are linked within one [32-day itinerary across eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

The tour also visits Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia. The selected four countries are neither consecutive nor a separate short tour: Montevideo is part of the Argentine stage, while Bolivia's and Peru's high-altitude days lie between Chile and Ecuador. This matters to travelers with limited time who want to visit specific cities and museums.

For the complete range, see the [Brazil–Chile–Ecuador–Uruguay selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile_ecuador_uruguay/). To compare culture-focused journeys including other countries, use the [multi-country culture and history catalog](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Brazil: Rio between colonial quarters and a modern state capital

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), two guided sightseeing excursions await. First, travelers ascend Corcovado to Christ the Redeemer; later they explore Sugarloaf Mountain and central districts. Historic churches, monasteries, colonial-era buildings and [Saint Sebastian's Metropolitan Cathedral](/brazil/place/rio-metropolitan-cathedral/) are of particular historical interest.

The city's heritage is seen against mountains and ocean. However, famous panoramas should not be confused with the number of museums visited: the principal format is general sightseeing, not a dedicated multi-day Brazilian art course. The itinerary then continues to [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), whose main appeal is natural. Optional activities at the waterfalls should not be counted as part of a cultural excursion just because the stops are in Brazil.

## Uruguay: Montevideo as a one-day introduction to a port city's history

You arrive in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) by ferry from Buenos Aires. The journey from Argentina begins in the morning, and a return ferry follows the sightseeing tour and free time. This is not a long stay in Uruguay: **one day is allocated to its capital**.

With an English-speaking guide, travelers visit [Montevideo Port](/uruguay/place/montevideo-port/), [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/), the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and [the cathedral](/uruguay/place/montevideo-cathedral/). The city introduces the culture of the Río de la Plata, shaped by its port history, public squares and preserved historic buildings.

For planning, allow for the ferry schedule, border formalities and actual walking time. The [Montevideo day trip from Buenos Aires](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/) includes ferry tickets but does not promise visits to all the capital's museums. Free time is limited by the return departure. Those who want to discover Uruguay in more depth need an additional program.

## Chile: La Moneda, Plaza de Armas and a city beside the Andes

The next cultural stage is [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The program includes a group sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide. It covers [La Moneda Palace](/chile/place/la-moneda-palace/), [Plaza de Armas](/chile/place/santiago-plaza-de-armas/), central government buildings, the cathedral and Santa Lucía Hill. Travelers also discover Santiago's modern districts.

This is the history of a nation that developed from a colonial city plan into a republican capital. The square and palace make the changes visible in architecture and urban space. The view from Santa Lucía adds the panorama of the city to that cultural context.

An excursion to wineries in the Maipo Valley, including tasting, is offered separately **for an additional fee**. The principal cultural day focuses on Santiago. The route then runs via Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and onward into Bolivia. Tiwanaku, visited later in Bolivia, must not be presented as a Chilean attraction merely because it belongs to the same long journey.

## Ecuador: historic Quito and the geography of the equator

Travelers arrive in Ecuador after days in Bolivia and Peru. In [Quito](/ecuador/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/quito-panecillo-and-equator/), the focus is the historic center: colonial streets, churches, architecture and Quito's artistic school. The sightseeing tour includes a panorama from El Panecillo.

The group then visits [Mitad del Mundo](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/) and the Intiñan Museum. These places provide a way to explore geodetic research, ideas about the equator and the region's cultural traditions. Museum demonstrations of physical effects should, however, be understood as part of an exhibition rather than as a replacement for scientific explanations of water movement or Earth's geography.

After Quito comes the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Here the focus changes to nature and wildlife observation. The marine excursion day includes only one of two alternatives: North Seymour with Bachas or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. An extensive historic or museum program should not be promised on islands whose actual itinerary centers on wildlife.

## What connects these countries and what sets them apart

| Country | Cultural focus |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Churches and old Rio |
| Uruguay | Port and historic Montevideo |
| Chile | Santiago's squares and palaces |
| Ecuador | Colonial Quito and the equator |

The actual travel order matters more than the nominal order in the selection title. Montevideo is visited via Buenos Aires, Santiago comes later, and Bolivia and Peru lie between the Chilean and Ecuadorian stages. Peru also includes Cusco and Machu Picchu: they are part of the cultural experience of **the full tour**, although Peru is not one of the four countries in this filter.

Guide languages differ by stage. Montevideo has an English-speaking guide, whereas Santiago's city tour uses a Russian-speaking guide. Compare each excursion's language and length, journey time and possible museum or church closures when choosing. Ada Tours helps coordinate the itinerary, while entry and re-entry requirements between Argentina and Uruguay are checked for each traveler's documents.

## Frequently asked questions about the historical route

### How many days are spent in Uruguay?

One excursion day in Montevideo on the current itinerary. Travelers arrive by ferry from Buenos Aires and return to Argentina the same day.

### Is there a tour of Santiago's historic center?

Yes. The group sightseeing program with a Russian-speaking guide includes La Moneda, Plaza de Armas and other city landmarks.

### Are ancient Inca monuments visited?

Yes, but in Peru, which belongs to the full eight-country route, not to this four-country selection. Cusco and a day trip to Machu Picchu are included.

### Can we limit the trip to Brazil, Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay?

The available tour in this selection visits all eight countries. A shortened four-country version would require separate agreement on city sequence, flights and duration.

### What language is the Montevideo excursion conducted in?

The current program specifies an English-speaking guide. Alternative guide languages would need to be arranged separately.

lead: >-
  The Brazilian side of Iguazu, the dry landscapes near San Pedro de Atacama and the volcanic Galápagos Islands reveal very different parts of South America's natural world. Uruguay features a one-day visit to Montevideo. All these stops belong to a 32-day tour, not to a separate itinerary covering just four countries.
---

## Brazil, Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay: combining waterfalls, desert and islands

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through [Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/), [Ecuador](/ecuador/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/). It is a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Besides the four selected nations, the itinerary includes Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia.

Nature plays different roles in these countries. Brazil includes a full excursion to Iguazu; Chile's itinerary takes travelers to the desert highlands of San Pedro de Atacama, mainly in preparation for Bolivia; Ecuador offers an island stage in the Galápagos. Uruguay is a sightseeing visit to Montevideo. This provides a striking contrast between landscapes, but the Nature theme does not make every excursion a nature excursion.

## Brazil: humid forest and Iguazu's cascades

The Brazilian section starts in São Paulo and continues to Rio de Janeiro, Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain. Mountains, the bay and forested slopes can be seen here, but the excursions are predominantly sightseeing: visits to the city's famous viewpoints and walks around old Rio.

Brazil's main nature day is at [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). A guided group excursion to the Brazilian side of the waterfalls with a Russian-speaking guide is included. Subtropical forest surrounds the cascades. UNESCO recognizes the natural importance of Iguaçu National Park and its relationship with the protected area across the Argentine border.

The source program names visits to the Bird Park and Macuco Safari as **optional**, not included, with separate prices. This is an important budget detail if you specifically want a boat trip near the waterfalls. The Argentine side of Iguazu and a flight to Buenos Aires follow. Visitors experience one major natural area from two sides, not two independent waterfall systems.

## Uruguay: the Río de la Plata waterfront for one day

After sightseeing in Buenos Aires, travelers take a ferry to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). The program includes an English-speaking guide, free time and a return to the Argentine capital the same day. Ferry tickets are included; an overnight stay in Uruguay is not specified.

Montevideo faces the broad waters of the Río de la Plata. Uruguay's Ministry of Tourism describes the rambla as an important urban promenade. Yet the itinerary does not include a separate tour of a Uruguayan nature park, ocean coastline or wetlands. For nature enthusiasts, it is therefore **a short city interlude**, not another major wildlife experience after Iguazu.

The ferry crossing is important to the route and documentation even though the day is mainly devoted to city sightseeing. Allow for an early departure from Buenos Aires and the return that evening.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama and acclimatization before Bolivia

Following Uruguay and the Argentine stops, the tour reaches [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and then flies to Calama for a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). According to the official Chile Travel portal, San Pedro lies in an area of dry desert and high-altitude scenery, including valleys and salt formations.

However, on the current 32-day itinerary, **this Chilean stage is described primarily as a transfer and acclimatization** before continuing into Bolivia. Visits to Moon Valley, El Tatio geysers or a separate astronomy night must not automatically be treated as included. The last is listed as an optional activity with a separate cost.

The next scheduled nature section begins on Bolivian territory: 4×4 vehicles, lagoons, thermal areas and the Uyuni Salt Flat. The Chilean scenery matters to the overall experience, but some of the actual landmarks lie **in Bolivia**, not Chile. Keeping this distinction clear avoids an inaccurate description of the route.

## Ecuador: the Galápagos as the main island nature experience

After Bolivia and Peru, travelers arrive in Quito and continue to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The plan includes Baltra, [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), the island's highlands and Puerto Ayora. This is a distinct nature experience that cannot be replaced with a general description of Ecuadorian tropical beaches.

The following island day includes **one of two alternatives**: North Seymour with Bachas or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. Neither branch is compulsory until the booking option is confirmed. UNESCO describes the Galápagos as a young volcanic archipelago where geographical isolation helped unusual fauna and flora evolve. Specific wildlife observations depend on the selected island, weather and national park rules.

Iguazu and the Galápagos differ fundamentally. Iguazu centers on water and the rainforest around its great cascades. The Galápagos focus on island geology, coastal scenery and animals, with marine transport between sites. Neither guarantees sightings of any particular species.

## Seasonality, preparation and the complete journey

The journey is scheduled for **22 October – 22 November 2026** and lasts 32 days. It spans eight countries, with domestic flights, hotel changes, city activities and different kinds of excursions. Nature days are separated by long transport sections and cultural stops.

Prepare for humidity at Iguazu, dry air and changes in altitude at San Pedro de Atacama, and marine crossings and protected-area rules in the Galápagos. Access to particular sites, weather and the chosen island-excursion branch are determined for the actual dates. Documents must be checked against nationality for **the full eight-country journey**, not only the four countries in the filter.

An unfiltered list is in the [Brazil, Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/brazil_chile_ecuador_uruguay/). Other nature combinations are in the [multi-country nature travel selection](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Are there nature excursions in all four countries?

Brazil includes Iguazu and Ecuador includes the Galápagos. Chile's stage passes through desert landscapes but primarily involves a transfer and acclimatization. Uruguay is a one-day city visit to Montevideo.

### Can both Galápagos island programs be taken in one day?

The current tour includes one of two alternatives, not both. The specific excursion needs to be confirmed.

### Is Macuco Safari included in the price?

Macuco Safari is listed as an extra excursion with a separate charge. The guided visit to the Brazilian side of Iguazu remains included.

### Why is Bolivia's highland landscape mentioned in an article about Chile?

San Pedro de Atacama in Chile is used as a stop before the cross-border 4×4 journey. The lagoons and Uyuni themselves are in Bolivia: these are two different stages.

## Where wildlife is actually observed along the itinerary

Brazil, Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay are included in the [Eight South American Countries in 32 Days tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). This is **a four-country selection from an eight-country itinerary** under Wildlife and Safaris, not a separate journey limited to these four nations. The interest is supported by an included day of wildlife observation in the Galápagos. Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia are also part of the complete program.

The main nature stops within the selected four are Brazil's [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and Ecuador's [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Chile's section covers Santiago and the road through Atacama; Uruguay's is a day trip to Montevideo. Expecting a separate safari in every country would be inaccurate.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The comparison below shows the itinerary and travel conditions.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Brazil: tropical forest and the optional Bird Park

After [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), you head to [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The included excursion covers the Brazilian side with a Russian-speaking guide. The national park protects a substantial section of Atlantic rainforest, with diverse wildlife. However, the walk along the viewpoints is mainly about the waterfalls: **no sightings of particular wild animal species are guaranteed**.

An [excursion to the Bird Park](/brazil/foz-do-iguacu/parque-das-aves-tour/) can be added on request. It offers an organized opportunity to see birds in enclosures, distinct from spotting wild animals in their natural habitat. On the eight-country program, it **costs extra**. Another optional excursion, Macuco Safari, combines a trip to the river with a boat ride near the falls. Its main purpose is experiencing the river scenery, not searching for jaguars.

For wildlife-focused travelers, the distinction between visiting a national park, joining an extra Bird Park activity and actually watching wild animals is useful. Each format carries different expectations, limitations and conditions.

## Ecuador: the Galápagos and two alternative island itineraries

From [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), you fly to the Galápagos. After landing on Baltra, you head to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), visit its [highlands and lava tunnels](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) and stay in Puerto Ayora. Along the way, the landscape changes visibly from dry volcanic areas to greener vegetation on the island's higher ground.

The following day includes **only one marine excursion from two alternatives**:

- [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach: the program describes seabird colonies, frigatebirds, blue-footed boobies, sea lions and coastal plants.
- [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrión: an island walk near habitats of sea lions, land iguanas and seabirds, followed by a marine stop.

These are **options for one excursion day**, so a visit to both islands cannot be promised. The choice is confirmed after booking. Both are described separately in the [North Seymour excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/) and [South Plaza excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/), but only one is selected.

The Galápagos are known for a high proportion of endemic species. Protected-area visits follow strict rules: authorized nature guides, designated paths, distance from animals and no feeding. Before flying to the archipelago, visitors obtain a transit control card and undergo baggage biosecurity screening; a separate conservation fee applies. Exact fees and procedures depend on passenger category and date.

## Chile and Uruguay: important stops without separate safaris

In [Chile](/chile/), the itinerary includes [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The next high-altitude section toward Bolivia starts here. Chile adds desert scenery to the journey's natural contrasts. **There is no dedicated wildlife-watching excursion in the Chilean section of this tour.** The optional evening telescope outing is about astronomy.

In Uruguay, a ferry takes travelers from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) for city sightseeing before returning to Argentina. Ferry tickets are included. Old Town streets, Independence Square and the capital's history are the focus. No national parks or wildlife safaris are included in Uruguay's day.

The full eight-country route also includes Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons with flamingos. But Bolivia **is not one of the four countries in this selection**: those experiences must not be attributed to Chile or Uruguay. Reviewing the whole itinerary is essential for assessing its wildlife content.

## Logistics: why the four countries cannot simply be linked by a direct route

The actual order is Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. The Galápagos are far from the mainland stops and require a separate flight and island transfers. There are lengthy travel sections and high-altitude days between the nature excursions.

At Iguazu, clothing that protects against spray and rain is useful. In the Galápagos, wear footwear suitable for rocky paths, protect yourself from the sun and bring clothing for boat trips. Binoculars allow birdwatching without approaching the birds. Bolivia's and Peru's highlands require warmer clothing and acclimatization precautions. Altitude can affect well-being even for those primarily interested in island wildlife.

Flight connections, visas and transit rules must be checked **for all eight countries on the itinerary**, accounting for nationality, passports and any repeat entries. Ada Tours helps coordinate flights, excursion days and recovery time between stages, while the exact services are confirmed when selecting the program.

Other animal-focused journeys are available under [multi-country Wildlife and Safaris](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) and [wildlife-watching tours in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/). Other interests for the same geography appear in the [general Brazil–Chile–Ecuador–Uruguay selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile_ecuador_uruguay/). For waterfalls, forests and desert landscapes, see [the same countries under Nature](/multi-country/brazil_chile_ecuador_uruguay/interests/nature/).

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife on this journey

### Can North Seymour and South Plaza both be visited on one excursion day?

Not on this tour. **One** alternative is confirmed: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión.

### Are blue-footed boobies, iguanas and sea lions guaranteed?

No. Excursions enter their habitats, but actual sightings, weather and site access depend on natural conditions and park regulations.

### Are Iguazu's Bird Park and Macuco Safari included?

They are offered as optional paid excursions. The Brazilian-side waterfalls excursion is included.

### Is there wildlife observation in Uruguay?

The Uruguayan day is devoted to urban Montevideo. No separate visit to a nature reserve is scheduled.

### Can these four countries be chosen while skipping the others?

The ready-made tour covers eight countries. Omitting some countries would require revising the route, cost, flights and included excursions.

Ada Tours' ready-made journeys include other essential stops between these countries: Argentina, and on longer routes Bolivia and Uyuni. ## Brazil, Chile and Peru: three distinct South American regions on one journey

Brazil, Chile and Peru offer an unusual combination of nature and culture: the Atlantic Ocean, tropical waterfalls, the Chilean Andes and ancient Inca cities. But the distance from [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is too great for short daily transfers. To spend time at the attractions themselves, flights and the sequence of stops have to be planned in advance.

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Brazil, Chile and Peru on the main route. **Every currently available qualifying tour also includes Argentina**, and most include Bolivia. This is important for planning: country-combination pages should not be mistaken for confirmed itineraries limited to the three named nations. Reducing a ready-made trip to only three countries would require a separate agreement on the route, flights, price and services.

Most journeys begin in Brazil, continue through the Argentine side of Iguazu and Buenos Aires, travel to Chile and finish in Peru. On longer programs, Bolivia's Uyuni Salt Flat and Lake Titicaca lie between Chile and Peru. This additional section makes the greatest difference to altitude demands and transport logistics.

## Brazil: the ocean, Corcovado and Iguazu Falls

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the journey usually begins with city highlights: Copacabana and Ipanema beaches, granite peaks rising above the city, Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado. Already, the experience differs sharply from Peru: a humid Atlantic coastline, tropical vegetation and sightseeing at lower elevations.

The route then proceeds to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). On the Brazilian side, travelers see wide panoramas of the falls; on the [Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), they explore other cascades and the Devil's Throat. This involves visiting two countries, not one excursion without a border crossing. Valid entry documents are required for both sides, and admission tickets and inclusions should be checked for each individual tour.

On the longer itineraries, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) follows Iguazu, with city tours and tango experiences. This explains why the Brazil–Chile–Peru combination currently refers to itineraries involving at least four countries. Removing Argentina would change both transport and the substance of the trip.

Event-based journeys bring another constraint. New Year in Rio takes place during the Southern Hemisphere summer, often with heat and high humidity. Carnival follows its own calendar. In both cases, conditions in Peru and Chile are those of the event's fixed season, rather than a specially chosen dry month in the Andes.

## Chile: Santiago alone, or Atacama as well?

The Chilean stage of the 15-day program includes [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and a visit to the Pacific coast at Valparaíso and Viña del Mar. Travelers explore historic and modern urban areas, Andean panoramas and coastal culture. In this option, Chile is mainly a city and coastline section between Argentina and Peru.

The 18- and 19-day routes also include [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). From there, excursions may visit [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) and other desert sites, then continue to Bolivia's highland regions. Road days become longer and may require off-road transport and early departures.

**Santiago and Atacama have different climates.** Clothing suited to walking around the capital may be inadequate for cold mornings in the desert or on a high-altitude plateau. Even in warmer seasons, prepare for sunshine, wind and large temperature changes.

Each entry to Chile requires a separate SAG agricultural declaration. Plant and animal products, including some food and souvenirs, must be declared. An inspector decides whether individual goods may enter, and crossing without a declaration may lead to penalties. This particularly matters on longer journeys with purchases still in the luggage from Brazil, Argentina or Bolivia.

## Peru: Cusco's altitude and Machu Picchu tickets

In the listed programs, Peru includes [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). These destinations have different geographical conditions and cannot be planned as one short sightseeing trip.

Cusco stands at around 3,350 m. If previous days were spent in Brazil, Buenos Aires or Santiago, a sudden move to this elevation may affect well-being. Assess acclimatization by the rate of ascent, altitude of overnight stays and available rest time, not simply by fitness.

Machu Picchu tickets are sold through Peru's Ministry of Culture's official system, specifying a date, visiting circuit, route and entry time. Popular options require advance planning. An admission ticket does not automatically grant access to every trail and viewpoint, so the sightseeing itinerary must match the actual ticket purchased.

On longer five-country tours, travelers pass through Bolivia toward [Lake Titicaca and Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) before Cusco. This may provide additional time at altitude, but also entails lengthy drives and further border formalities. Here the shorter route without Bolivia differs most clearly from the expedition-style option.

## If Bolivia is included: Uyuni and lengthy transfers

On five-country routes, the Atacama stage is followed by travel across Bolivia's Altiplano, colorful lagoons, geyser fields and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The desert surface can be dry and white or partly covered with rainwater. The mirror effect depends on weather and road conditions, so it cannot be promised for any particular date.

Travelers then visit [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and the Titicaca region before entering Peru. Some sections are much higher than most travelers are accustomed to, with infrastructure far from large cities. Confirmed transportation, actual overnight stops, journey time and the possibility of road changes in poor conditions all matter.

**The Bolivian section changes the nature of the holiday as well as its length.** A city sightseeing walk can often be adjusted freely. A remote high-altitude road journey offers less flexibility, while road conditions and how the group feels become especially important. Travelers who struggle at altitude should assess the route in advance and discuss medical limitations with a doctor.

## When to travel: comparing three climate zones

Brazil around Rio and Iguazu is warm and humid, Santiago has Mediterranean seasonal patterns, and the month chosen for Cusco and Bolivia's Altiplano strongly affects rain and cold nights. **There is no single best season for all stages at once.**

| Section | Key factor |
|---|---|
| Rio and Iguazu | Heat, humidity, rain |
| Santiago | Summer warmth, winter cool |
| Cusco | Wet and dry months |
| Uyuni, if included | Water, road access, nighttime cold |

December to March is generally warm in Rio and Santiago, but wetter in the Peruvian Andes. Cusco and Machu Picchu may have cloud and heavy rainfall; road and trail conditions should be checked before travel. Choosing the Andean dry season, roughly May to September, changes weather conditions in Chile, and nights on Bolivia's plateau can be very cold.

The New Year itinerary in Rio is fixed to a particular calendar week. The Champions Parade also follows Carnival dates. If one of these events is your main reason for traveling, the season in the other countries is a fixed consequence rather than something that can be freely changed.

For the complete route, pack light clothes for Brazil, a waterproof layer, a warm jacket for the highlands, comfortable footwear and sun protection. Domestic-flight baggage rules can vary even within a single journey. Ticket conditions, the number of connections and carrier limitations matter.

## Documents, payments and connections between countries

Entry requirements for Brazil, Chile and Peru depend on nationality and the specific route. However, **every currently available combination includes Argentina**, and several include Bolivia. Visa checks must therefore cover the four or five countries actually visited. The Iguazu border crossing and the high-altitude transition from Chile into Bolivia deserve particular attention.

One journey may require Brazilian reals, Argentine pesos, Chilean pesos, Peruvian soles and, if Bolivia is included, bolivianos. Divide your personal-expense budget by country and payment type. Cards may be more convenient in cities, while remote places may require cash. Acceptance of international cards depends on the issuer and local restrictions; Russian bank-issued cards should not be assumed to work outside Russia.

For connections, compare the complete flight route: arrival and departure airports, baggage collection, transit rules and time needed for immigration. A high-altitude road journey or a visit to a remote natural site immediately before an international departure requires a buffer. An extra night in a major city may be preferable to linking a distant mountain transfer to a flight with no margin.

## Frequently asked questions about Brazil, Chile and Peru

### Is there a ready-made trip covering only these three countries?

All the currently listed qualifying tours also include Argentina, and most include Bolivia. A journey covering exactly three countries would require a customized itinerary with different flights and services.

### Can Rio and Machu Picchu be visited in two weeks?

Yes, with flights the combination is possible. Ada Tours' closest existing program lasts 15 days and covers four countries: Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru. Shortening the holiday or removing stops would change the itinerary.

### Should Machu Picchu be booked in advance?

Yes. Establish the date, visiting circuit and entry time first, then coordinate trains, transfers and accommodation around Cusco. The different visiting routes are not interchangeable.

### Why are clothing requirements so different within one journey?

Rio is on a warm, humid coast, Santiago has its own seasonal conditions, and Cusco, especially the Altiplano, experience strong sun and cold nights. Pack for the coldest and windiest section, not only the first stop.
